channel.title: Pier & Point · Pier 48
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Pier 48 (Mission Rock), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Pier 48: The Mission Rock environmental review analyzed a rehabilitation of Pier 48…
item.description: The Mission Rock environmental review analyzed a rehabilitation of Pier 48 (261,000 gsf in the 2016 historic resource evaluation, 242,500 gsf in the EIR project table), and the 2018 agreement lets it go forward only once a feasible pier use plan is developed. The Board of Supervisors approved the ten-year lease on February 13, 2018, at 66% of gross parking revenues less parking taxes and authorized extraordinary expenses; no later document confirming the lease is still in force was found. Phase 1 anticipated 'as many as' 750 to 1,000 parking spaces. No source gives a start date for the current rehabilitation. Source: https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/r0043-18.pdf; https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Mission%20Rock%20Approvals%20Staff%20Report%201-26-18FINAL.pdf; https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/sfmea/MissionRock_Appendix%203-1_HistoricResourcesEvaluation.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Pier 48: Pier 48's record now states: built 1928-30 (not 1924-30)
item.description: Pier 48's record now states: built 1928-30 (not 1924-30); 261,000 gsf per the Historic Resource Evaluation (the 263,000 gsf and 33,800 gsf valley figures removed); the Tudor/Gothic Revival style applies to the bulkhead buildings, not the transit sheds; the 1,200-ft pier in the Biennial Report passage was Pier 45's, not Pier 48's; the Anchor Brewing announcement is dated February 2013 (ENR reported it on 2013-02-28 as made 'last week'); Anchor's 2024 buyer is described as working to restart the brewery, not as ruling out an SF brewery; 'not rehabilitated' and the statement about pile and seismic work are dated to the Port's Mission Rock page or removed; the Jan 30, 2018 approval now cites the Port Commission minutes; the 2013 valley photo is retagged as a document figure; and source titles for the 2012 Revised Proposal, the Design Controls and the 2018 press release were corrected. The dead sfplanning.org link is replaced by the readable copy of the Historic Resource Evaluation. Source: VerPlanck Historic Preservation Consulting, Historic Resource Evaluation, Seawall Lot 337 & Pier 48 (EIR Appendix 3-1), 2016-04-11 (https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/sfmea/MissionRock_Appendix%203-1_HistoricResourcesEvaluation.pdf); Engineering News-Record, 2013-02-28 (https://www.enr.com/blogs/14-gold-rush/post/16138-sf-s-anchor-brewing-pours-into-pier-48); The San Francisco Standard, 2024-05-31 (https://sfstandard.com/2024/05/31/anchor-brewing-sold-to-chobani-yogurt-king-yes-the-old-label-will-return/); Port of San Francisco, Mission Rock (https://www.sfport.com/projects-programs/mission-rock); Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download).
item.source: VerPlanck Historic Preservation Consulting, Historic Resource Evaluation, Seawall Lot 337 & Pier 48 (EIR Appendix 3-1), 2016-04-11 (https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/sfmea/MissionRock_Appendix%203-1_HistoricResourcesEvaluation.pdf); Engineering News-Record, 2013-02-28 (https://www.enr.com/blogs/14-gold-rush/post/16138-sf-s-anchor-brewing-pours-into-pier-48); The San Francisco Standard, 2024-05-31 (https://sfstandard.com/2024/05/31/anchor-brewing-sold-to-chobani-yogurt-king-yes-the-old-label-will-return/); Port of San Francisco, Mission Rock (https://www.sfport.com/projects-programs/mission-rock); Port of San Francisco, Minutes of the Special Port Commission Meeting, 2018-01-30 (https://www.sfport.com/media/3353/download)

item.title: Correction · Pier 48: Pier 48's record now sits under its corrected lot number, 8719A001, matching…
item.description: Pier 48's record now sits under its corrected lot number, 8719A001, matching the earlier lot correction. It had been left under the old identifier 9900048 and was not shown on the site until a site-build check caught it. No other content changed. Source: Pier & Point editorial decision.

item.title: Correction · Pier 48: Pier 48 moved to its live Assessor lot 8719A001
item.description: Pier 48 moved to its live Assessor lot 8719A001. The 9900048 lot it was joined to was retired on 2020-06-12 (per DataSF Parcels); 8719A001 was recorded the same day. Source: DataSF Parcels (lot dropped from the roll 2020-06-12).

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: The San Francisco Standard reports (article published this… (May 31, 2024)
item.description: The San Francisco Standard reports (article published this day; it gives no closing date) that Anchor Brewing and its 2.17-acre Potrero Hill home (501 De Haro St. brewery) have been bought by Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya's Shepherd Futures, which is working with developer Presidio Bay Ventures 'to help restart the brewery operations' (no Pier 48 plan mentioned) (May 31, 2024). Source: The San Francisco Standard, 2024-05-31.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: Anchor Brewing announces it is ceasing operations after 127… (Jul 12, 2023)
item.description: Anchor Brewing announces it is ceasing operations after 127 years (Jul 12, 2023). Source: KQED, 2023-07-12.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: Phase 1 submittal (submitted 7/2/2019) anticipates Pier 48… (Jul 2, 2019)
item.description: Phase 1 submittal (submitted 7/2/2019) anticipates Pier 48 parking of "as many as 750 to 1,000 spaces, pending demand and the use of valet operations" (Jul 2, 2019). Source: Mission Rock Partners (developer's submittal to the Port), 2019-07-02.
item.source: Mission Rock Partners (developer's submittal to the Port), 2019-07-02

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: Port issues a Request for Interest for public-oriented uses of… (Aug 1, 2018)
item.description: Port issues a Request for Interest for public-oriented uses of 13 historic piers from Pier 35 to Pier 48; responses due October 31, 2018 (Aug 1, 2018). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2018-08-01.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: Board of Supervisors approves the Pier 48 lease (Resolution… (Feb 13, 2018)
item.description: Board of Supervisors approves the Pier 48 lease (Resolution 43-18, File 180093, date passed February 13, 2018): base rent $55,416.47 a month April to September and $2,916.67 a month October to March, plus 66% of gross parking revenues less parking taxes and authorized, substantiated extraordinary expenses, ten-year term (Feb 13, 2018). Source: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, 2018-02.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 48: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA, which allows a… (Jan 30, 2018)
item.description: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA, which allows a Pier 48 rehabilitation to move forward "based on the parties' development of a feasible pier use plan" (the staff report's words), and a 10-year Pier 48 lease to China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events (Resolutions 18-03, 18-10) (Jan 30, 2018). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2018-01-30; Port of San Francisco, 2018-01-26.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2018-01-30; Port of San Francisco, 2018-01-26
